title: A task tracker library
description: Build a small task tracker as classes, with errors for misuse and a generator for listing. ```javascript const board = new Board(); const a = board.add("Write report", { priority: 2, tags: ["work"] }); // returns the new Task const b = board.add("Buy milk"); board.complete(b.id); [...board.tasks({ done: false })].map(t => t.title); // ["Write report"] board.summary(); // "1 of 2 done; next: Write report (priority 2)" ``` **`Task`** - Built by the board, not directly: `new Task(id, title, { priority = 3, tags = [] } = {})`. - Has read-only `id` and `title` (getters over private fields), `priority` (1 is the most urgent, up to 5), a copy of `tags`, and `done` (starts `false`). - `complete()` sets `done` to `true`; completing a task twice throws a `TaskError` with the message `already done`. - `toString()` gives `[x] Title (p2) #work #home` for a done task and `[ ] Title (p3)` without tags. **`TaskError extends Error`** with `name` set to `"TaskError"`. **`Board`** - `add(title, options)` trims the title and throws a `TaskError` `title is empty` when nothing is left, or `priority must be 1 to 5` for a priority that is not a whole number from 1 to 5. Ids are 1, 2, 3... in order of adding, per board. - `get(id)` returns the task or throws a `TaskError` `no task `. - `complete(id)` completes that task; `remove(id)` removes it (throws for unknown ids). - `*tasks({ done, tag } = {})` is a **generator** yielding tasks sorted by priority then id. `done: true/false` keeps only done or open tasks, and `tag` keeps only tasks with that tag. Leaving an option out means "any". - `summary()` returns `" of done; next: (priority <p>)"`, where next is the first open task in `tasks()` order. When nothing is open, it ends with `; nothing left` instead; with no tasks at all it is `"no tasks"`. - `toJSON()` returns a plain array of `{ id, title, priority, tags, done }` (so `JSON.stringify(board)` works), and the static `Board.fromJSON(text)` builds a board back from that text. The restored board continues with ids above the largest one.
hints: A static method can use private fields of the objects of its own class: inside `fromJSON`, `board.#tasks` is allowed.
In `tasks()`, sort a copy of the values once, then `yield` each task that passes both filters; `done !== undefined` tells whether the option was given.
requirements: Private fields (`#`) for each task's id and title and for the board's storage.
A `TaskError` class used for every misuse.
`toJSON` and a static `fromJSON` for saving and loading.
stretch: Add `board.undo()`, which reverses the last `add`, `complete` or `remove`.
